_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-09 18:34:11Z)**_

答案是：**沒有全域設定 `GOBIN=~/.local/bin`**。我在 repo 裡找到的完整情況如下。

## 現況

全域（shell 層）只設了 `GOPATH`，沒設 `GOBIN`。在 `dot_config/shell/02_legacy_tools.sh:9-10`：

```sh
export GOPATH="${GOPATH:-$HOME/go}"
[[ -d "$GOPATH/bin" ]] && export PATH="$GOPATH/bin:$PATH"
```

`GOBIN=~/.local/bin` 只在兩個**範圍受限**的地方出現，都不是全域 export：

| 位置 | 作用範圍 |
|---|---|
| `dot_ansible/roles/go_tools/tasks/main.yml:43` | 只在 ansible 跑 `go install` 那個 task 的 `environment:` 內 |
| `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh:542` | 只在 `just upgrade-go` 的升級流程內 |

也就是說：**受管的** go 工具（go_tools role + upgrade 腳本）會乖乖裝進 `~/.local/bin`；但你在 shell 裡**手動** `go install` 時，GOBIN 不會是 `~/.local/bin`。

## 這台機器的實際狀態

```
GOPATH   = /Users/david/go
GOBIN    = /Users/david/.local/share/mise/installs/go/1.26.4/bin   ← mise shim 注入的
GOMODCACHE = /Users/david/go/pkg/mod
```

兩個值得注意的點：

1. **手動 `go install` 目前會落到 mise 的版號目錄**（`~/.local/share/mise/installs/go/1.26.4/bin`），不是 `~/go/bin` 也不是 `~/.local/bin`。這其實比 `~/go/bin` 更糟一點——它綁在 go 版本上，`go` 一升版整個目錄就被換掉，裝的 CLI 就消失了。這也是為什麼 `~/go/bin` 目前不存在。

2. **`~/go` 還是被建出來了**——因為 `GOPATH=~/go`，module cache 預設在 `$GOPATH/pkg/mod`，所以 `~/go/pkg/mod` 一定會生成（`~/go` 和 `~/go/pkg` 現在都在）。就算把 GOBIN 設好，光靠 GOBIN 也清不掉這個 `~/go`。

## 如果你想讓 home 真的乾淨

要達成你說的「避免 home 有 `~/go`」，需要兩件事一起做，加在 `02_legacy_tools.sh` 的 Go 區塊：

```sh
export GOPATH="${GOPATH:-$XDG_DATA_HOME/go}"   # ~/.local/share/go，消掉 ~/go

I searched the web for recommended practices around Go’s GOBIN/GOPATH and the XDG ~/.local/bin location. Below are the concise findings and a short, actionable recommendation you can apply.

Key findings
- If GOPATH is unset, Go defaults GOPATH to $HOME/go. ([go.dev](https://go.dev/wiki/SettingGOPATH))  
- go install writes executables to GOBIN; if GOBIN is not set it defaults to GOPATH/bin (so, e.g., $HOME/go/bin). Setting GOBIN overrides that destination. ([stackoverflow.com](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/40067997/how-to-set-gobin-automatically))  
- The XDG Base Directory spec and common distro guidance treat ~/.local/bin as the standard per-user location for user-installed executables. Many tutorials and blogs recommend using ~/.local/bin for user-level installs so you don’t need sudo and your home remains tidy. ([specifications.freedesktop.org](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/basedir/latest/))  
- With Go modules (modern Go), you rarely need to fiddle with GOPATH for dependency management; however the install location for tool binaries still follows the GOBIN/GOPATH/bin rules above. ([gofaq.org](https://www.gofaq.org/en/how-to-use-go-install-to-install-binaries/))

Recommended, simple best-practice (what many users do)
1. Put user-installed Go binaries into ~/.local/bin (XDG-friendly) and ensure that directory is in your PATH. This avoids sudo and matches the XDG convention. ([specifications.freedesktop.org](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/basedir/latest/))  
2. Set GOBIN to that directory (optional, but explicit):  
   - mkdir -p ~/.local/bin  
   - export GOBIN="$HOME/.local/bin"  
   - export PATH="$GOBIN:$PATH"  
   Or instead of exporting GOBIN you can add the default GOPATH/bin to PATH (export PATH="$HOME/go/bin:$PATH") if you prefer the Go default. ([stackoverflow.com](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/40067997/how-to-set-gobin-automatically))
3. Do not normally set GOROOT; only set it if you installed Go in a nonstandard location. ([programming-books.io](https://www.programming-books.io/essential/go/gopath-goroot-gobin-d6da4b8481f94757bae43be1fdfa9e73))
4. Use the module-aware form of go install for tools (go install package@version) if you want reproducible installs; the resulting binary will land in GOBIN or GOPATH/bin as above. ([gofaq.org](https://www.gofaq.org/en/how-to-use-go-install-to-install-binaries/))

Notes / trade-offs
- Using ~/.local/bin is portable across Linux distributions and matches XDG guidance; some existing Go tutorials still assume $HOME/go/bin — both are fine if you add the appropriate directory to PATH. ([specifications.freedesktop.org](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/basedir/latest/))  
- If you manage multiple Go versions or system-wide tools, you may prefer /usr/local/bin (requires sudo) or a version manager; for per-user convenience ~/.local/bin is usually simplest. ([guillermodotn.github.io](https://guillermodotn.github.io/posts/Where_to_manually_install_your_programs_on_linux/))

- The build cache (GOCACHE) is separate from the module cache and, if GOCACHE is not explicitly set, Go prefers XDG_CACHE_HOME (then $HOME/.cache) when computing the default build-cache location. Practical examples (Unix-like shells)
- Show current values:
  - go env GOMODCACHE
  - go env GOCACHE
  - go env GOPATH
  (these will print what the go command is currently using). ([pkg.go.dev](https://pkg.go.dev/cmd/go?utm_source=openai))

- Temporarily (for current shell):
  - export GOMODCACHE="${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/go/pkg/mod"
  - export GOCACHE="${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/go-build"  (optional; GOCACHE will already choose XDG_CACHE_HOME by default if unset). ([go.dev](https://go.dev/src/cmd/go/testdata/script/cache_unix.txt?utm_source=openai))

- Persistently for the go tool (recommended if you want the go command to remember it):
  - go env -w GOMODCACHE="$HOME/.cache/go/pkg/mod"
  - go env -w GOCACHE="$HOME/.cache/go-build"  (only if you want to override the default behavior). ([pkg.go.dev](https://pkg.go.dev/cmd/go?utm_source=openai))

Notes and gotchas
- GOMODCACHE controls only the module cache (downloaded module source). It does not change the build cache (GOCACHE) or other Go directories (GOBIN, GOPATH unless you set them). Use GOCACHE to control the build cache. ([go.dev](https://go.dev/ref/mod?utm_source=openai))  
- The go tool’s default cache discovery is OS-aware: on Unix-like systems it prefers XDG_CACHE_HOME (or $HOME/.cache), while Windows and some other OSes use their platform-specific locations. - If you set both GOPATH and GOMODCACHE, GOMODCACHE is used for the module cache. If neither GOMODCACHE nor GOPATH is set, some go commands will error (module cache not found). ([go.dev](https://go.dev/src/cmd/go/testdata/script/mod_gomodcache.txt?utm_source=openai))

I searched official Go docs and community Q&A about go env -w, the GOENV file location, and how go env -w differs from exporting in the shell.

Short summary / answers
- The persistent file that go env -w writes to is the GOENV file, located at os.UserConfigDir() + "/go/env". That resolves to platform defaults:
  - Linux / Unix: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/go/env if set, otherwise $HOME/.config/go/env. ([go.googlesource.com](https://go.googlesource.com/proposal/%2B/master/design/30411-env.md))  
  - macOS: $HOME/Library/Application Support/go/env. ([stackoverflow.com](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/40825613/where-are-the-golang-environment-variables-stored))  
  - Windows: %APPDATA%\go\env (i.e., the user roaming AppData\go\env). ([go.googlesource.com](https://go.googlesource.com/proposal/%2B/master/design/30411-env.md))

- go env -w writes key=value settings into that file so the go tool uses them as persistent defaults. You can see the effective path with go env GOENV. ([go.dev](https://go.dev/doc/manage-install))

- Shell exports (export VAR=val / setx / $env:VAR=...) are process/OS environment variables and take precedence over values stored with go env -w. In other words: if an environment variable is present in the process environment, it overrides the GOENV file value. Use export for temporary/session settings; use go env -w to set a persistent default for the go command when no process env value is present. ([stackoverflow.com](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/77332596/whats-the-difference-between-export-and-go-env-w))

- You cannot set the GOENV location itself with go env -w (go env -w GOENV=...) — the go command rejects changing GOENV that way. If you want to change where the go command looks for its env file, set the GOENV environment variable in your OS/shell (export GOENV=path on Unix, setx or $env:GOENV on Windows). ([go.dev](https://go.dev/src/cmd/go/testdata/script/env_write.txt?m=text))

Useful commands/examples
- Show the active GOENV path and other values:
  - go env GOENV; go env GOPRIVATE (or any variable)
- Persist a Go setting:
  - go env -w GOPRIVATE=example.com
- Temporarily override in your shell:
  - export GOPRIVATE=example.com  (Unix)
  - setx GOPRIVATE example.com  (Windows, persistent for future shells)
  - $env:GOPRIVATE = 'example.com'  (PowerShell, current session)
- To change where the go tool reads its env file (example, Unix):
  - export GOENV=/some/path/to/env  (must be set in OS/shell; cannot use go env -w)

Sources (selected)
- Go project design / proposal: command configuration stored in os.UserConfigDir()+"/go/env". ([go.googlesource.com](https://go.googlesource.com/proposal/%2B/master/design/30411-env.md))  
- Go docs — user config / managing installs (notes that Go stores user config under os.UserConfigDir and that go env GOENV shows the config-file path). ([go.dev](https://go.dev/doc/manage-install))

 `./dot_config/shell/02_legacy_tools.sh`

```text
1	# 02_legacy_tools.sh - Legacy tools and PATH configurations (POSIX subset).
2	# Sourced by both ~/.zshrc and ~/.bashrc via load_modular_dir
3	# "$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/shell" sh. Tools that existed before chezmoi management;
4	# kept for backwards compatibility with existing installations.
5	
6	# =============================================================================
7	# Go (Golang)
8	# =============================================================================
9	export GOPATH="${GOPATH:-$HOME/go}"
10	[[ -d "$GOPATH/bin" ]] && export PATH="$GOPATH/bin:$PATH"
11	
12	# Homebrew Go (Apple Silicon, then Intel), falling back to a manual /usr/local/go
13	# install only when neither brew Go exists. Order matters: the Intel brew path
14	# (/usr/local/opt/go/bin) MUST come before the manual /usr/local/go fallback, or
15	# a stale hand-installed Go (e.g. an old go1.15 from a 2020 .pkg) shadows brew's
16	# current Go on Intel Macs. See memory: homebrew-aliyun-autoupdate-hang.
17	if [[ -d "/opt/homebrew/opt/go/bin" ]]; then
18	    export PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/go/bin:$PATH"
19	elif [[ -d "/usr/local/opt/go/bin" ]]; then
20	    export PATH="/usr/local/opt/go/bin:$PATH"
21	elif [[ -d "/usr/local/go/bin" ]]; then
22	    export PATH="/usr/local/go/bin:$PATH"
23	fi
24	
25	# =============================================================================
26	# Bun (JavaScript runtime)
27	# https://bun.sh/
28	# =============================================================================
29	export BUN_INSTALL="${BUN_INSTALL:-$HOME/.bun}"
30	[[ -d "$BUN_INSTALL/bin" ]] && export PATH="$BUN_INSTALL/bin:$PATH"
31	# bun's ~/.bun/_bun is a ZSH-only completion file (uses zsh glob qualifiers
32	# like `(N)` and the `_alternative` builtin) that errors loudly when sourced
33	# in bash. Gate to zsh; bash gets bun completion via bash-completion v2 if
34	# bun installed it under $HB_PREFIX/etc/bash_completion.d/ instead.
35	if [ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ] && [ -s "$BUN_INSTALL/_bun" ]; then
36	    source "$BUN_INSTALL/_bun"
37	fi
38	
39	# =============================================================================
40	# pnpm (package manager)
41	# https://pnpm.io/
42	# =============================================================================
43	if [[ "$OSTYPE" == darwin* ]]; then
44	    export PNPM_HOME="${PNPM_HOME:-$HOME/Library/pnpm}"
45	else
46	    export PNPM_HOME="${PNPM_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share/pnpm}"
47	fi
48	[[ -d "$PNPM_HOME" ]] && export PATH="$PNPM_HOME:$PATH"
49	
50	# =============================================================================
51	# Foundry (Ethereum development toolkit)
52	# https://getfoundry.sh/
53	# =============================================================================
54	[[ -d "$HOME/.foundry/bin" ]] && export PATH="$HOME/.foundry/bin:$PATH"
55	
56	# =============================================================================
57	# NVM (Node Version Manager) - Legacy
58	# https://github.com/nvm-sh/nvm
59	# NOTE: mise (05_mise.zsh) is preferred for Node.js management.
60	#       nvm is skipped by default. Use `LOAD_NVM=1 zsh` or add to ~/.zshrc.adhoc.
61	# =============================================================================
62	export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
63	
64	if [[ -n "$LOAD_NVM" ]]; then
65	    [ -s "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" ] && \. "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh"
66	    [ -s "$NVM_DIR/bash_completion" ] && \. "$NVM_DIR/bash_completion"
67	fi
68	
69	# =============================================================================
70	# .NET
71	# =============================================================================
72	[[ -d "$HOME/.dotnet/tools" ]] && export PATH="$HOME/.dotnet/tools:$PATH"
73

 `./backlog/bin-migration.md`

```text
1	# Relocate `~/bin/` to a chezmoi-distinct path
2	
3	**Status**: Done 2026-05-13 — relocated to `~/.dotfiles/bin/` (namespace anchor variant, NOT the `~/.dotfiles-bin/` flat layout originally recommended below).
4	**Effort**: M (actual: source rename + 12 doc/config references + transitional PATH)
5	**Related**: `dot_dotfiles/bin/`, `dot_config/shell/00_exports.sh.tmpl:21-26`, `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`, `docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md`
6	
7	## Resolution (2026-05-13)
8	
9	Chosen target: **`~/.dotfiles/bin/`** — `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_*` in source.
10	
11	**Why the namespace variant won over the flat `~/.dotfiles-bin/`**: user signalled
12	extensibility intent — "這種設計 可能也可以把一些通用的 scripts/ 放過去" — so
13	future `~/.dotfiles/scripts/`, `~/.dotfiles/lib/`, etc. can grow as siblings inside
14	the one namespace anchor instead of proliferating top-level hidden dirs
15	(`~/.dotfiles-bin/`, `~/.dotfiles-lib/`, ...). The name is also tool-agnostic
16	(no chezmoi-coupling) so renaming the toolchain later doesn't make the path lie.
17	
18	**Transitional PATH**: `$HOME/.dotfiles/bin:$HOME/bin:$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH`.
19	`$HOME/bin` stays in PATH for one personal sync cycle so any hand-placed
20	`~/bin/<x>` files keep resolving. After every host has applied the new layout
21	AND the user has cleaned up old `~/bin/{sms,mi-router,x,sesh-preview,fleet}`,
22	a follow-up commit drops `$HOME/bin` from PATH entirely.
23	
24	**Cleanup is manual** (intentionally not automated via run-script): chezmoi
25	doesn't own non-chezmoi `~/bin/<x>` entries, and an auto-rm could surprise a
26	user with a same-named binary they placed there. Per host:
27	
28	```
29	rm ~/bin/{sms,mi-router,x,sesh-preview,fleet}
30	rmdir ~/bin 2>/dev/null  # only succeeds if dir is empty
31	```
32	
33	## Original context (preserved for reference)
34	
35	Surfaced 2026-05-13 while adding `bin/executable_fleet` (the umbrella `fleet`
36	CLI). Currently `bin/executable_*` files in chezmoi deploy to `~/bin/`:
37	
38	```
39	bin/executable_sms           → ~/bin/sms
40	bin/executable_mi-router     → ~/bin/mi-router
41	bin/executable_x             → ~/bin/x   (also documented at ~/.local/bin/x)
42	bin/executable_sesh-preview  → ~/bin/sesh-preview
43	bin/executable_fleet         → ~/bin/fleet  (post 2026-05)
44	```
45	
46	`~/bin` is a collision-prone target — third-party installers (Anaconda, asdf,
47	mise, custom build scripts) sometimes drop binaries there or expect it as
48	user-writable scratch space. With 5 chezmoi-managed entries and growing, "where
49	did this binary come from" is harder to answer than it should be.
50	
51	User question (paraphrased): "can we rename `~/bin` to a more hidden path that
52	doesn't mix with `~/.local/bin` (which is for auto-installed `uv tool` / `cargo
53	install` / `mise` output), so it's obvious these are chezmoi-managed?"
54	
55	## Options
56	
57	| Option | Pros | Cons |
58	|---|---|---|
59	| **Stay at `~/bin/`** (current) | Zero migration cost; widely understood convention | Collision risk persists; mixes with non-chezmoi binaries |
60	| **`~/.dotfiles-bin/`** | Prefix telegraphs origin; clean isolation from `.local/bin` | Non-standard XDG; needs PATH update + every doc update |
61	| **`~/.local/share/chezmoi-bin/`** | XDG-aligned ("data" under chezmoi); explicit ownership | `share/` is conventionally for non-executable data; long path |
62	
63	Recommended (if/when migrated): `~/.dotfiles-bin/` — the prefix is the whole
64	point, and `.local/share/` for executables is unusual enough to surprise
65	future contributors.
66	
67	## Files affected by any migration
68	
69	- `bin/executable_sms` / `mi-router` / `x` / `sesh-preview` / `fleet` — rename
70	  the source dir (`bin/` → e.g. `dot_dotfiles-bin/`)
71	- `dot_config/shell/00_exports.sh.tmpl:23` — PATH export (`$HOME/bin:$HOME/.local/bin`)
72	- `justfile` — audit for `~/bin` hardcodes (none today, but the new `fleet`
73	  recipe calls the source path, not the deployed binary, so no change required
74	  if the source dir is renamed too)
75	- `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md` — references to `~/bin/fleet`
76	- `docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md:199` — the `~/.local/bin/x` aspirational note
77	- `pitfalls/*.md` — audit before migrating (none reference `~/bin` today)
78	- `bootstrap.sh` / `Dockerfile` if they mention PATH
79	
80	## Migration ordering (when revisited)
81	
82	1. Add new path to PATH alongside the old one (so `~/bin/sms` keeps working
83	   while the new `~/.dotfiles-bin/sms` is being adopted).
84	2. `chezmoi apply` deploys to the new path on every host (fleet-apply handles
85	   the rollout).
86	3. Flip every doc reference to the new path.
87	4. Wait one release / one personal sync cycle so all machines are up.
88	5. Remove the old `~/bin/` entries by hand on each host (or via a one-shot
89	   `run_onchange_after_*.sh.tmpl` that `rm`s the known set of legacy
90	   filenames — careful not to remove user-created `~/bin/*`).
91	
92	## Decision
93	
94	Deferred until either:
95	- A real collision happens (e.g. asdf-installed `sms` overrides chezmoi's), or
96	- `bin/` exceeds ~10 entries (currently 5).
97	
98	The bin-migration risk (5 binaries × PATH × every doc reference) is
99	uncorrelated with the value of any single new binary; bundling them
100	into a feature commit expands the blast radius for no upside.
101	
102	## Reference
103	
104	- Original discussion: 2026-05-13, fleet-CLI session — user raised the
105	  question while approving the umbrella `fleet` binary plan.
106	- Plan file at the time: `.claude/plans/fleet-scripts-fleet-apply-py-cli-bin-jazzy-glacier.md`
107
```

- When you use the @version suffix, go install runs in module-aware mode and ignores the current module's go.mod (it resolves the specified module/version independently). ([go.googlesource.com](https://go.googlesource.com/go/%2B/go1.16/src/cmd/go/testdata/script/mod_install_pkg_version.txt?autodive=0%2F%2F%2F&utm_source=openai))

- go install accepts multiple package arguments with version suffixes only under strict conditions: all arguments must refer to packages that are provided by the same module at the same version. If versions differ or packages come from different modules, go install reports errors (e.g., “all arguments must refer to packages in the same module at the same version”). Wildcards only match main packages. ([go.dev](https://go.dev/src/cmd/go/testdata/script/mod_install_pkg_version.txt?utm_source=openai))

- Common error cases shown in Go’s test data:
  - Passing different version suffixes or packages from different modules causes explicit errors.  
  - Passing a non-main package will error (“package ... is not a main package”).  
  These behaviors are exercised in the Go project’s test scripts. ([go.dev](https://go.dev/src/cmd/go/testdata/script/mod_install_pkg_version.txt?utm_source=openai))

- For managing developer tools in your home/dotfiles, common approaches are:
  - Set GOBIN (or GOPATH/bin) and use go install pkg@version to place binaries there. ([go.dev](https://go.dev/doc/manage-install?utm_source=openai))

To eliminate ambiguity about which module versions are used in the build, if any of the arguments have version suffixes, the arguments must satisfy the following constraints:

    * Arguments must be package paths or package patterns (with “`...`” wildcards). They must not be standard packages (like `fmt`), meta-patterns (`std`, `cmd`, `all`, `work`, `tool`), or relative or absolute file paths. Note that `go install tool` can be used without a version suffix: see below.
    * All arguments must have the same version suffix. Different queries are not allowed, even if they refer to the same version.

    * Package path arguments must refer to `main` packages. Pattern arguments will only match `main` packages.
    * No module is considered the [main module](#glos-main-module).

        * The module must not require a higher version of itself.
        * Vendor directories are not used in any module. (Vendor directories are not included in [module zip files](#zip-files), so `go install` does not download them.)"

Some prefer keeping it under DATA (GOPATH/pkg/mod) to avoid re-downloads. The Arch Wiki and community consensus lean toward the CACHE approach, which is what I'll recommend, while noting this trade-off.

# Go env layout for a tidy HOME — decision-ready summary

**Quick verdict:** Move `GOPATH` to `$XDG_DATA_HOME/go`, point `GOBIN` at `~/.local/bin`, and optionally move the module cache to `$XDG_CACHE_HOME`. Go does *not* do any of this by default (GOPATH is still hardcoded to `~/go`), but every one of these vars is officially settable and this is a well-worn community pattern. There is one macOS-specific gotcha (below) that matters since you're on Darwin.

## 1. GOBIN

- **What it does / default:** `go install` writes executables (main packages) to `GOBIN`. If unset, it defaults to `$GOPATH/bin`, i.e. `$HOME/go/bin` when GOPATH is also unset. ([go.dev/ref/mod](https://go.dev/ref/mod), [go.dev/doc/manage-install](https://go.dev/doc/manage-install))
- **`GOBIN=~/.local/bin` — good practice? Yes.** `~/.local/bin` is the XDG-conventional per-user executable dir and is very commonly already on `PATH`. Setting `GOBIN` there is a standard, recommended way to keep `~/go/bin` from existing at all.
- **Does `go install pkg@version` respect GOBIN? Yes.** The module-aware `pkg@version` form installs to `GOBIN` (or `$GOPATH/bin`) exactly like the classic form. ([go.dev/ref/mod](https://go.dev/ref/mod), [go.dev/doc/manage-install](https://go.dev/doc/manage-install))
- **Known caveats / errors:**
  - **Cross-compiling with GOBIN set fails.** If `GOOS`/`GOARCH` differ from the host and `GOBIN` is set, a plain `go install` errors with `cannot install cross-compiled binaries when GOBIN is set`. This is an intentional check in the go tool (it otherwise disambiguates by writing to `$GOPATH/bin/<goos>_<goarch>/`, which it can't do inside a single fixed GOBIN). Workaround: `go build -o <path>`, or unset GOBIN for that build. ([cmd/go/internal/work/build.go](https://go.dev/src/cmd/go/internal/work/build.go), [SO #37503085](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/37503085/building-for-arm-cannot-do-cross-compilation-with-go-install-when-gobin-is-se))
  - The multi-argument restrictions you're thinking of ("all arguments must refer to packages in the same module at the same version", must be `main` packages, etc.) are a property of the `pkg@version` **module-aware** form, *not* of GOBIN — they apply whether or not GOBIN is set. ([go.dev/ref/mod](https://go.dev/ref/mod))
- **Is a mixed dir (non-Go binaries) safe? Yes.** `go install` only creates/overwrites the specific binaries it builds; it never enumerates, cleans, or manages the directory. Pointing GOBIN at a shared `~/.local/bin` full of other tools is safe and standard.

## 2. GOPATH relocation

- **Safe and supported** to move it out of `~/go` via `export GOPATH=...` or `go env -w GOPATH=...`. Default is `$HOME/go`. ([go.dev/wiki/SettingGOPATH](https://go.dev/wiki/SettingGOPATH), [go.dev/doc/articles/go_command](https://go.dev/doc/articles/go_command))
- **What still lives under GOPATH in module mode (Go 1.16+):**
  - `$GOPATH/pkg/mod` — the **module cache** (downloaded module source), unless `GOMODCACHE` is set.
  - `$GOPATH/pkg/mod/cache/download` — the module *download* cache, including `.../sumdb/` (the **checksum database cache**) and `cache/lock`.
  - `$GOPATH/bin` — installed binaries, unless `GOBIN` is set.
  - (Legacy `$GOPATH/src` is only relevant to old GOPATH-mode workflows.)
- **What breaks if you move it:** essentially nothing in module mode, provided you update `PATH` if you rely on `$GOPATH/bin`. GOPATH can be a list; the *first* entry is where `go install`/downloads go. The only things that "break" are legacy GOPATH-mode `go get`/`src`-tree workflows, which are largely irrelevant post-1.16.

## 3. GOMODCACHE

- **Independent of GOPATH? Yes** (since Go 1.15). Defaults to `$GOPATH/pkg/mod`; you can override it alone via env or `go env -w GOMODCACHE=...`. ([go.dev/ref/mod](https://go.dev/ref/mod), [pkg.go.dev/cmd/go](https://pkg.go.dev/cmd/go))
- **Relocating to XDG is common but not officially "blessed"** — Go's own default keeps it under GOPATH; the community pattern (Arch Wiki / dotfiles) puts it under `$XDG_CACHE_HOME`. It works fine.
- **Gotchas:**
  - Module cache files/dirs are created **read-only** by design. Don't `rm -rf` it — use **`go clean -modcache`** (the supported way to wipe it). ([go.dev/ref/mod](https://go.dev/ref/mod))
  - `-modcacherw` (Go 1.14+) makes newly-created cache dirs writable if you need to delete/edit manually, at the cost of accidental-modification protection. ([go.dev/doc/go1.14](https://go.dev/doc/go1.14), [go.dev/wiki/Modules](https://go.dev/wiki/Modules))
  - Windows/AV can cause "Access is denied" on cleanup (golang/go#36568) — not your concern on Darwin.

## 4. Go and XDG Base Directory

- **Already XDG-compliant by default (on Linux):**
  - **`GOENV`** (the `go env -w` file) lives at `os.UserConfigDir()/go/env` → `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/go/env`, i.e. `~/.config/go/env` on Linux. ([proposal 30411-env](https://go.googlesource.com/proposal/+/master/design/30411-env.md))
  - **`GOCACHE`** (build cache, separate from the module cache) defaults to `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/go-build` → `~/.cache/go-build` on Linux. ([cmd/go cache_unix test](https://go.dev/src/cmd/go/testdata/script/cache_unix.txt))
- **NOT XDG by default:** `GOPATH` (`~/go`), `GOMODCACHE` (`$GOPATH/pkg/mod`), `GOBIN` (`$GOPATH/bin`). These are what create HOME clutter, and Go deliberately keeps `GOPATH=$HOME/go` (golang/go#17262). ([#17262](https://github.com/golang/go/issues/17262))
- **Native "full XDG support" status as of 2026: not happening.** There is no accepted proposal to relocate GOPATH / module cache to XDG by default. The most relevant tracked proposal, **golang/go#62382** (`os.UserDataDir` / `os.DataDir` stdlib helpers), was **closed as "not planned"** (opened Aug 2023). Related env-file work #57179 (load `$GOROOT/go.env` before the user file) is also closed and does *not* touch GOPATH/cache XDG placement. So the story is: config + build cache already honor the platform config/cache dir; everything else you set yourself. ([#62382](https://github.com/golang/go/issues/62382), [#57179](https://github.com/golang/go/issues/57179))
- **`go env -w` vs shell `export`:**
  - `go env -w KEY=val` writes a persistent default into the **GOENV file**; it affects **only the go tool**, and is overridden by any process env var of the same name. Precedence: **process env > GOENV file > built-in default.** ([SO #77332596](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/77332596/whats-the-difference-between-export-and-go-env-w))
  - `export` sets a real process env var: higher precedence, and **visible to all programs** (your shell, editors, other tools that read `GOPATH`/`GOBIN`), not just `go`. For dotfiles that other tooling also reads, prefer `export`. You **cannot** set `GOENV` itself via `go env -w` — it must be a real env var. ([SO #40825613](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/40825613/where-are-the-golang-environment-variables-stored))

### ⚠️ macOS caveat (you're on Darwin)
Go's platform dirs on macOS are **Apple's, not XDG**: `os.UserConfigDir()` = `~/Library/Application Support` and `os.UserCacheDir()` = `~/Library/Caches`, and Go does **not** consult `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`/`XDG_CACHE_HOME` on darwin. So by default on your machine:
- `GOENV` → `~/Library/Application Support/go/env` (not `~/.config`)
- `GOCACHE` → `~/Library/Caches/go-build` (not `~/.cache`)

If you want a uniform `~/.config` / `~/.cache` / `~/.local/share` layout on macOS, you must set `GOENV`, `GOCACHE`, `GOMODCACHE`, `GOPATH`, and `GOBIN` **explicitly** — the XDG defaults won't kick in for you the way they do on Linux. ([SO #40825613](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/40825613/where-are-the-golang-environment-variables-stored))

## 5. Recommended canonical layout

Community consensus (XDG-tidy HOME), expressed as shell `export`s so other tools see them too:

```sh
export GOPATH="${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/go"
export GOMODCACHE="${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/go/mod"   # optional; see trade-off
export GOBIN="$HOME/.local/bin"                              # ensure it's on PATH
export GOCACHE="${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/go/build"    # needed on macOS; Linux already does this
# Optional, macOS only, if you want the env file under ~/.config:
export GOENV="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/go/env"
```

Net effect: `~/go` never gets created; binaries land in the `~/.local/bin` you already have on PATH; caches live under `~/.cache`; module source lives under `~/.cache/go/mod` (or `~/.local/share/go/pkg/mod` if you drop `GOMODCACHE`).

**Trade-offs to decide:**

- **GOBIN: `~/.local/bin` vs `$XDG_DATA_HOME/go/bin`.** `~/.local/bin` is the better choice for a tidy HOME — it's the standard user-bin dir, usually already on PATH, and mixing non-Go binaries there is safe. `$XDG_DATA_HOME/go/bin` keeps Go stuff self-contained but adds another PATH entry. Most tidy-HOME setups use `~/.local/bin`.
- **Module cache in CACHE (`~/.cache`) vs DATA (`~/.local/share`).** This is the main judgment call:
  - *In `$XDG_CACHE_HOME`* (set `GOMODCACHE`): "cache-y" dir; some cleaners (e.g. tools that periodically purge `~/.cache`) may delete it. **This is safe for correctness** — the module cache is content-addressed and checksum-verified against `go.sum`/GONOSUMDB, so Go just re-downloads. The only cost is bandwidth/time on the next build.
  - *In `$XDG_DATA_HOME`* (leave `GOMODCACHE` unset so it stays `$GOPATH/pkg/mod` = `~/.local/share/go/pkg/mod`): survives cache purges, no surprise re-downloads, at the price of a larger "data" dir that won't be auto-reclaimed.
  - Recommendation: if you run cache cleaners, `$XDG_CACHE_HOME` is fine and arguably semantically correct. If you value never re-downloading modules offline, leave it under `$XDG_DATA_HOME/go`. Either way, clean it with `go clean -modcache`, not `rm -rf` (read-only files).
- **`export` vs `go env -w`.** Use `export` in your dotfiles for `GOPATH`/`GOBIN`/`GOMODCACHE` since editors, LSPs, and other tools read those too. Reserve `go env -w` for go-only knobs (e.g. `GOFLAGS`, `GOPRIVATE`). Remember env `export` wins over the GOENV file.
- **Cross-compiling.** With `GOBIN` set, remember `go install` refuses cross-compiled binaries — use `go build -o` for those. Rarely an issue for day-to-day tool installs.

# Go env layout for a tidy HOME — decision-ready summary

**Quick verdict:** Move `GOPATH` to `$XDG_DATA_HOME/go`, point `GOBIN` at `~/.local/bin`, and optionally move the module cache to `$XDG_CACHE_HOME`. Go does *not* do any of this by default (GOPATH is still hardcoded to `~/go`), but every one of these vars is officially settable and this is a well-worn community pattern. There is one macOS-specific gotcha (below) that matters since you're on Darwin.

## 1. GOBIN

- **What it does / default:** `go install` writes executables (main packages) to `GOBIN`. If unset, it defaults to `$GOPATH/bin`, i.e. `$HOME/go/bin` when GOPATH is also unset. ([go.dev/ref/mod](https://go.dev/ref/mod), [go.dev/doc/manage-install](https://go.dev/doc/manage-install))
- **`GOBIN=~/.local/bin` — good practice? Yes.** `~/.local/bin` is the XDG-conventional per-user executable dir and is very commonly already on `PATH`. Setting `GOBIN` there is a standard, recommended way to keep `~/go/bin` from existing at all.
- **Does `go install pkg@version` respect GOBIN? Yes.** The module-aware `pkg@version` form installs to `GOBIN` (or `$GOPATH/bin`) exactly like the classic form. ([go.dev/ref/mod](https://go.dev/ref/mod), [go.dev/doc/manage-install](https://go.dev/doc/manage-install))
- **Known caveats / errors:**
  - **Cross-compiling with GOBIN set fails.** If `GOOS`/`GOARCH` differ from the host and `GOBIN` is set, a plain `go install` errors with `cannot install cross-compiled binaries when GOBIN is set`. This is an intentional check in the go tool (it otherwise disambiguates by writing to `$GOPATH/bin/&lt;goos&gt;_&lt;goarch&gt;/`, which it can't do inside a single fixed GOBIN). Workaround: `go build -o &lt;path&gt;`, or unset GOBIN for that build. ([cmd/go/internal/work/build.go](https://go.dev/src/cmd/go/internal/work/build.go), [SO #37503085](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/37503085/building-for-arm-cannot-do-cross-compilation-with-go-install-when-gobin-is-se))
  - The multi-argument restrictions you're thinking of ("all arguments must refer to packages in the same module at the same version", must be `main` packages, etc.) are a property of the `pkg@version` **module-aware** form, *not* of GOBIN — they apply whether or not GOBIN is set. ([go.dev/ref/mod](https://go.dev/ref/mod))
- **Is a mixed dir (non-Go binaries) safe? Yes.** `go install` only creates/overwrites the specific binaries it builds; it never enumerates, cleans, or manages the directory. Pointing GOBIN at a shared `~/.local/bin` full of other tools is safe and standard.

## 2. GOPATH relocation

- **Safe and supported** to move it out of `~/go` via `export GOPATH=...` or `go env -w GOPATH=...`. Default is `$HOME/go`. ([go.dev/wiki/SettingGOPATH](https://go.dev/wiki/SettingGOPATH), [go.dev/doc/articles/go_command](https://go.dev/doc/articles/go_command))
- **What still lives under GOPATH in module mode (Go 1.16+):**
  - `$GOPATH/pkg/mod` — the **module cache** (downloaded module source), unless `GOMODCACHE` is set.
  - `$GOPATH/pkg/mod/cache/download` — the module *download* cache, including `.../sumdb/` (the **checksum database cache**) and `cache/lock`.
  - `$GOPATH/bin` — installed binaries, unless `GOBIN` is set.
  - (Legacy `$GOPATH/src` is only relevant to old GOPATH-mode workflows.)
- **What breaks if you move it:** essentially nothing in module mode, provided you update `PATH` if you rely on `$GOPATH/bin`. GOPATH can be a list; the *first* entry is where `go install`/downloads go. The only things that "break" are legacy GOPATH-mode `go get`/`src`-tree workflows, which are largely irrelevant post-1.16.

## 3. GOMODCACHE

- **Independent of GOPATH? Yes** (since Go 1.15). Defaults to `$GOPATH/pkg/mod`; you can override it alone via env or `go env -w GOMODCACHE=...`. ([go.dev/ref/mod](https://go.dev/ref/mod), [pkg.go.dev/cmd/go](https://pkg.go.dev/cmd/go))
- **Relocating to XDG is common but not officially "blessed"** — Go's own default keeps it under GOPATH; the community pattern (Arch Wiki / dotfiles) puts it under `$XDG_CACHE_HOME`. It works fine.
- **Gotchas:**
  - Module cache files/dirs are created **read-only** by design. Don't `rm -rf` it — use **`go clean -modcache`** (the supported way to wipe it). ([go.dev/ref/mod](https://go.dev/ref/mod))
  - `-modcacherw` (Go 1.14+) makes newly-created cache dirs writable if you need to delete/edit manually, at the cost of accidental-modification protection. ([go.dev/doc/go1.14](https://go.dev/doc/go1.14), [go.dev/wiki/Modules](https://go.dev/wiki/Modules))
  - Windows/AV can cause "Access is denied" on cleanup (golang/go#36568) — not your concern on Darwin.

```md
# Tidy Go env vars — banish `~/go` from HOME

## Context

`go install` and Go's module cache currently clutter `$HOME` with a `~/go` tree.
On this Mac today: `GOPATH=~/go` (so `~/go/pkg/mod` exists), and interactive
`go install` resolves `GOBIN` to the **mise version-pinned toolchain dir**
(`~/.local/share/mise/installs/go/<ver>/bin`) — which gets wiped on every Go
version bump, silently losing installed CLIs.

Meanwhile the repo's automation **already** standardizes on `GOBIN=~/.local/bin`
(the "blessed dir", already on PATH) in `go_tools` role + `upgrade_tools.sh` — but
the interactive shell was never brought in line, and neither automation path sets
`GOPATH`, so a build-time module cache still recreates `~/go`.

**Goal (best-practice, user-approved scope):** make `~/go` never appear again.
Move `GOPATH` to the XDG data dir and pin `GOBIN=~/.local/bin` consistently across
**all three** Go-install surfaces (shell, ansible, upgrade). Module cache then lives
at `~/.local/share/go/pkg/mod` (data dir — survives `~/.cache` cleaners). `GOCACHE`
(build cache) stays at Go's macOS-native `~/Library/Caches/go-build` — under
`~/Library`, not clutter, left untouched by design.

Research basis: Go does **not** honor XDG for `GOPATH`/`GOBIN`/`GOMODCACHE` by
default (golang/go#17262, closed) and ignores `XDG_*` entirely on darwin; every
one of these vars is officially settable via `export`, and `go install pkg@version`
honors `GOBIN`. `export` (not `go env -w`) is correct here so editors/LSPs also see
the values.

## Changes

### 1. `dot_config/shell/02_legacy_tools.sh` — interactive shells (primary)

Replace the Go section (lines 6–10, the `## Go` header block down to the
`$GOPATH/bin` PATH line — **leave the toolchain PATH block at lines 17–23 intact**):

\```sh
# =============================================================================
# Go (Golang) — keep HOME tidy: no ~/go. GOPATH → XDG data, go install → ~/.local/bin.
# XDG_DATA_HOME is exported by the rc files before this module (defensive fallback
# kept per repo convention). ~/.local/bin is already on PATH via 00_exports.sh.tmpl,
# so GOBIN targets need no extra PATH entry. GOCACHE stays macOS-native (~/Library).
# =============================================================================
export GOPATH="${GOPATH:-${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/go}"
export GOBIN="${GOBIN:-$HOME/.local/bin}"
\```

- Drop the old `[[ -d "$GOPATH/bin" ]] && export PATH="$GOPATH/bin:$PATH"` line: with
  `GOBIN` set, `$GOPATH/bin` is never populated, and `~/.local/bin` is already on PATH
  (`dot_config/shell/00_exports.sh.tmpl:26`). Removing it avoids a misleading dead entry.
- Keep the `${GOPATH:-…}` / `${GOBIN:-…}` guards so a user override in
  `~/.shellrc.adhoc` / secrets still wins (matches every other module here).
- File is plain `.sh` (POSIX, both shells) — no templating; the `${XDG_..:-…}`
  fallback covers macOS + Linux identically.

### 2. `dot_ansible/roles/go_tools/tasks/main.yml` — add `GOPATH` to the install task

The `Install Go CLI tools via go install` task (`:34-44`) sets `GOBIN` but **not**
`GOPATH`, so its build-time module cache lands in the default `~/go/pkg/mod`.
Add one line to the task's `environment:` (next to the existing `GOBIN:` at `:43`):

\```yaml
    GOPATH: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/share/go"
\```

Matches the existing hardcoded-`HOME` style in that block (ansible env doesn't carry
`XDG_DATA_HOME`).

### 3. `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh` — `cat_go()` set `GOPATH` alongside `GOBIN`

At `:542`, next to `export GOBIN="$HOME/.local/bin"`, add:

\```sh
  export GOPATH="$HOME/.local/share/go"
\```

Same reason: the upgrade re-install must not repopulate `~/go/pkg/mod`.

### 4. Docs — `docs/this_repo/config-conventions.md` § E1 PATH table (+ zh-TW mirror)

The `| ~/go/bin/ | Go | go install targets |` row (`:275`) is now false.
- Fold Go into the `~/.local/bin/` row (`:273`): "Auto-installed CLIs (uv, mise,
  chezmoi, just, fd, eza, **go install**, …)".
- Replace the `~/go/bin/` row with a note (or drop it and add a one-liner under the
  table): GOPATH now lives at `~/.local/share/go`; `go install` → `~/.local/bin`;
  module cache → `~/.local/share/go/pkg/mod`.
- Mirror the same edit in `docs/this_repo/config-conventions.zh-TW.md:245-246`.

**No change needed** (verified consistent): `docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md:587-588`
and `docs/this_repo/upgrades.md:53` already describe GOBIN→`~/.local/bin`. `aliases.md`
is alias/function-scoped — a plain `export` doesn't belong there. `architecture.md`'s
tier note doesn't hardcode `~/go`, so it isn't made stale (its pre-existing GOPATH
mislabel under `00_exports` is out of scope).

## One-time manual cleanup (documented, NOT automated)

After apply + verify, the orphaned `~/go` can be removed. Module cache files are
created **read-only** by Go, so `rm -rf` alone can choke — use one of:

\```sh
GOPATH="$HOME/go" go clean -modcache   # supported way to wipe the old cache
rmdir ~/go/bin ~/go/pkg ~/go 2>/dev/null || { chmod -R u+w ~/go && rm -rf ~/go; }
\```

Left manual on purpose — never auto-`rm` a user data dir.

## Verification (per repo "validate with the app" invariant)

1. `chezmoi diff dot_config/shell/02_legacy_tools.sh` → review; `chezmoi apply`.
2. Open a **new** shell, then:
   \```sh
   go env GOPATH GOBIN GOMODCACHE GOCACHE
   #   GOPATH     = ~/.local/share/go
   #   GOBIN      = ~/.local/bin
   #   GOMODCACHE = ~/.local/share/go/pkg/mod   (derived from GOPATH)
   #   GOCACHE    = ~/Library/Caches/go-build    (macOS-native, unchanged)
   \```
   Confirms the mise-shim GOBIN override is gone.
3. Functional install:
   \```sh
   go install golang.org/x/tools/cmd/goimports@latest
   command -v goimports        # -> ~/.local/bin/goimports, runnable
   ls ~/go 2>/dev/null && echo "REGRESSION: ~/go recreated" || echo "ok: no ~/go"
   ls ~/.local/share/go/pkg/mod   # module cache landed in XDG data
   \```
4. Ansible surface: the `go_tools` install task has a `creates:` guard, so removing a
   managed binary (e.g. `rm ~/.local/bin/<tool>`) then re-running the role (or the
   `just` go_tools path) should reinstall it into `~/.local/bin` with **no** `~/go`.
   At minimum `ansible-playbook --syntax-check` the role and eyeball the rendered
   `environment:`.
5. Upgrade surface: `just upgrade-go` (reinstalls at `@latest`) → binaries in
   `~/.local/bin`, `~/go` not recreated.
6. Cross-platform sanity: the plain-`.sh` + `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-…}` fallback means the
   same block works on Linux (where XDG is native) — no template branch to test.

## Caveats to keep in mind

- **Cross-compiling + GOBIN set**: `go install` refuses cross-compiled binaries when
  `GOBIN` is set (`cannot install cross-compiled binaries when GOBIN is set`). Use
  `go build -o <path>` for those. Rare for day-to-day tool installs.
- **macOS ignores XDG for Go**: `GOCACHE`/`GOENV` stay under `~/Library` on this Mac
  by design (user chose not to force them to XDG) — intentional, not a gap.

The `Install Go CLI tools via go install` task (`:34-44`) sets `GOBIN` but **not**
`GOPATH`, so its build-time module cache lands in the default `~/go/pkg/mod`.
Add one line to the task's `environment:` (next to the existing `GOBIN:` at `:43`):

```yaml
    GOPATH: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/share/go"
```

Matches the existing hardcoded-`HOME` style in that block (ansible env doesn't carry
`XDG_DATA_HOME`).

### 3. `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh` — `cat_go()` set `GOPATH` alongside `GOBIN`

At `:542`, next to `export GOBIN="$HOME/.local/bin"`, add:

```sh
  export GOPATH="$HOME/.local/share/go"
```

Same reason: the upgrade re-install must not repopulate `~/go/pkg/mod`.

### 4. Docs — `docs/this_repo/config-conventions.md` § E1 PATH table (+ zh-TW mirror)

The `| ~/go/bin/ | Go | go install targets |` row (`:275`) is now false.
- Fold Go into the `~/.local/bin/` row (`:273`): "Auto-installed CLIs (uv, mise,
  chezmoi, just, fd, eza, **go install**, …)".
- Replace the `~/go/bin/` row with a note (or drop it and add a one-liner under the
  table): GOPATH now lives at `~/.local/share/go`; `go install` → `~/.local/bin`;
  module cache → `~/.local/share/go/pkg/mod`.
- Mirror the same edit in `docs/this_repo/config-conventions.zh-TW.md:245-246`.

**No change needed** (verified consistent): `docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md:587-588`
and `docs/this_repo/upgrades.md:53` already describe GOBIN→`~/.local/bin`. `aliases.md`
is alias/function-scoped — a plain `export` doesn't belong there. `architecture.md`'s
tier note doesn't hardcode `~/go`, so it isn't made stale (its pre-existing GOPATH
mislabel under `00_exports` is out of scope).

## One-time manual cleanup (documented, NOT automated)

After apply + verify, the orphaned `~/go` can be removed. Module cache files are
created **read-only** by Go, so `rm -rf` alone can choke — use one of:

```sh
GOPATH="$HOME/go" go clean -modcache   # supported way to wipe the old cache
rmdir ~/go/bin ~/go/pkg ~/go 2>/dev/null || { chmod -R u+w ~/go && rm -rf ~/go; }
```

Left manual on purpose — never auto-`rm` a user data dir.

## Verification (per repo "validate with the app" invariant)

1. `chezmoi diff dot_config/shell/02_legacy_tools.sh` → review; `chezmoi apply`.
2. Open a **new** shell, then:
   ```sh
   go env GOPATH GOBIN GOMODCACHE GOCACHE
   #   GOPATH     = ~/.local/share/go
   #   GOBIN      = ~/.local/bin
   #   GOMODCACHE = ~/.local/share/go/pkg/mod   (derived from GOPATH)
   #   GOCACHE    = ~/Library/Caches/go-build    (macOS-native, unchanged)
   ```
   Confirms the mise-shim GOBIN override is gone.
3. Functional install:
   ```sh
   go install golang.org/x/tools/cmd/goimports@latest
   command -v goimports        # -> ~/.local/bin/goimports, runnable
   ls ~/go 2>/dev/null && echo "REGRESSION: ~/go recreated" || echo "ok: no ~/go"
   ls ~/.local/share/go/pkg/mod   # module cache landed in XDG data
   ```
4. Ansible surface: the `go_tools` install task has a `creates:` guard, so removing a
   managed binary (e.g. `rm ~/.local/bin/<tool>`) then re-running the role (or the
   `just` go_tools path) should reinstall it into `~/.local/bin` with **no** `~/go`.
   At minimum `ansible-playbook --syntax-check` the role and eyeball the rendered
   `environment:`.
5. Upgrade surface: `just upgrade-go` (reinstalls at `@latest`) → binaries in
   `~/.local/bin`, `~/go` not recreated.
6. Cross-platform sanity: the plain-`.sh` + `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-…}` fallback means the
   same block works on Linux (where XDG is native) — no template branch to test.

## Caveats to keep in mind

- **Cross-compiling + GOBIN set**: `go install` refuses cross-compiled binaries when
  `GOBIN` is set (`cannot install cross-compiled binaries when GOBIN is set`). Use
  `go build -o <path>` for those. Rare for day-to-day tool installs.
- **macOS ignores XDG for Go**: `GOCACHE`/`GOENV` stay under `~/Library` on this Mac
  by design (user chose not to force them to XDG) — intentional, not a gap.
```

11	## Pitfalls vs the rest
12	
13	This repo has four sibling surfaces with overlapping shapes; pick the right one:
14	
15	| Surface | Time direction | Question it answers | Access pattern |
16	|---|---|---|---|
17	| `docs/tools/<tool>.md` | Present | "How does this tool work / how do I configure it?" | Read top to bottom |
18	| `docs/this_repo/<topic>.md` | Present | "Why did we architect it this way?" | Read top to bottom |
19	| `pitfalls/<slug>.md` | **Past** | **"I see error X — has this happened before?"** | **Grep symptoms** |
20	| `backlog/<slug>.md` | Future | "We thought about doing Y — what was the analysis?" | Index in `TODO.md` |
21	| `AGENTS.md` Hard invariants | Present | "What rules MUST agents follow?" | Read top to bottom |
22	
23	A pitfall **graduates** to a Hard invariant in `AGENTS.md` when the trap is
24	serious enough that you can't rely on memory or grep — typically when (a) it
25	recurs across machines, (b) it silently corrupts state, or (c) the workaround
26	is non-obvious and easy to undo by accident. When graduating, leave a
27	`pitfalls/<slug>.md` as historical record and link to it from the invariant.
28	
29	## When to add a pitfall doc
30	
31	Add a `pitfalls/<slug>.md` when you've spent more than ~15 minutes on something
32	where the answer wasn't googleable, AND any of:
33	
34	- The symptom is non-obvious from the root cause (`SSH_CONNECTION` cleared
35	  silently → hostname module disappears, no error)
36	- The fix is "do nothing different but in a specific order" (sentinel writes
37	  must come after `wait $pid` for fleet-apply, etc.)
38	- The same trap could be hit by a new agent / new machine / new contributor
39	- An upstream bug exists with no ETA — workaround needs to outlive memory
40	- A specific tool version is required (or forbidden) and the failure mode at
41	  the wrong version is silent / confusing (e.g. tmux 3.2a popup off-screen)
42	
43	## When NOT to add a pitfall doc
44	
45	- Trivially googleable error (the next person will solve in 30 seconds anyway)
46	- Already covered in `docs/tools/<tool>.md` as part of the tool's normal
47	  configuration — cross-link from this README's "Cross-referenced pitfalls"
48	  table below instead of duplicating
49	- Already a `AGENTS.md` Hard invariant — those have higher priority enforcement
50	  (cross-link only)
51	- One-off transient (network glitch, machine-specific config rot) — fix and

167	## Cross-referenced pitfalls (still in their original homes)
168	
169	These traps are documented elsewhere and aren't duplicated here — the table
170	exists so grepping `pitfalls/` still finds them. Move into this folder only
171	if their original location stops being a natural reading flow.
172	
173	| Trap | Lives in | Why not here |
174	|---|---|---|
175	| chezmoi `modify_` files clobbered by `chezmoi add` | `docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md` → "Case studies in this repo" | Already part of the prefix-semantics narrative |

```md
# `go install` targets the mise toolchain dir, not ~/.local/bin — GOBIN keeps resetting

**Symptoms** (grep this section):
- `go env GOBIN` returns `/Users/<you>/.local/share/mise/installs/go/<ver>/bin` (or Linux `~/.local/share/mise/installs/go/<ver>/bin`) instead of `~/.local/bin`
- CLIs installed with `go install …@latest` silently **disappear after a `go` version bump** (mise upgrades Go → old `installs/go/<oldver>/bin` is removed → the binaries went with it)
- `export GOBIN="$HOME/.local/bin"` in your shell rc **does not stick**: correct right after the export, but reverts to the mise dir after the next `cd`
- `mise env -s zsh` prints `export GOBIN=/…/mise/installs/go/<ver>/bin` and `export GOROOT=…`
- `mise settings ls --all | grep -i go` lists `go_set_gopath` and `go_set_goroot` but there is **no `go_set_gobin`**

**First seen**: 2026-07
**Affects**: mise (all versions incl. 2026.2.5) managing Go on macOS + Linux; any host where `go` is a mise tool
**Status**: fixed in-repo (override `GOBIN` in mise's own `[env]`)

## Symptom

On a mise-managed Go, `go install` writes into the version-pinned toolchain dir:

\```
$ go env GOBIN
/Users/david/.local/share/mise/installs/go/1.26.4/bin
\```

Setting it from the shell looks like it works, then silently loses on the next prompt:

\```
$ export GOBIN="$HOME/.local/bin"; echo $GOBIN
/Users/david/.local/bin
$ cd /tmp && cd -
$ echo $GOBIN
/Users/david/.local/share/mise/installs/go/1.26.4/bin   # reverted
\```

The practical damage: every `go install`'d CLI lives under `installs/go/<ver>/bin`,
so `mise upgrade go` (or `go = "latest"` picking up a new release) wipes them all.

## Root cause

mise's Go backend **force-exports `GOBIN` (and `GOROOT`)** pointing at the active
toolchain's `bin`, and mise's shell activation re-asserts its env via `hook-env` on
**every directory change** — so it clobbers any plain shell `export` that ran earlier
in the rc. Unlike `GOPATH` (which mise leaves alone when `go_set_gopath=false`, its
default), there is **no `go_set_gobin` setting** to turn the GOBIN injection off.

`go env -w GOBIN=…` doesn't help either: a process env var (which mise sets) beats the
`go env` config file in Go's precedence order (env > GOENV file > built-in default).

## Workaround

Override `GOBIN` in **mise's own `[env]` table** — it is applied by the same
`hook-env` pass and takes precedence over the backend's default GOBIN, so it survives
`cd`. In `dot_config/mise/config.toml.tmpl`:

\```toml
[env]
GOBIN = "{{ .chezmoi.homeDir }}/.local/bin"
\```

Verify (fresh interactive shell, then a `cd` round-trip):

\```
$ go env GOBIN            # -> ~/.local/bin
$ cd /tmp && cd -; go env GOBIN   # still ~/.local/bin
\```

`GOPATH` does **not** need this treatment — mise ships `go_set_gopath=false`, so a
shell `export GOPATH=…` (dot_config/shell/02_legacy_tools.sh) is stable across `cd`.

## Prevention

When mise manages a tool that force-sets env vars with no `*_set_*` toggle, the shell
rc is the wrong layer — put the override in mise `[env]` so it wins the `hook-env`
race. For Go specifically, `dot_config/shell/02_legacy_tools.sh` still exports
`GOBIN`/`GOPATH` as the **non-mise fallback** (hosts without mise-managed Go), but the
mise `[env]` block is the authority whenever mise is active.

## Related

- `dot_config/mise/config.toml.tmpl` — the `[env] GOBIN` override
- `dot_config/shell/02_legacy_tools.sh` — shell fallback (GOPATH + GOBIN with `:-` guards)
- `docs/this_repo/config-conventions.md` § E1 — PATH dir table (`~/.local/share/go` GOPATH row)
- Upstream: mise Go backend sets GOROOT/GOBIN; only `go_set_gopath` / `go_set_goroot` are exposed

完成並驗證。`~/go` 已從 HOME 消失，而且驗證時發現原計畫沒料到的根因，多修了一處。

## 結果（實測）
在乾淨的新 shell 裡 `go env`：
- `GOPATH = ~/.local/share/go`
- `GOBIN = ~/.local/bin`（**`cd` 來回後仍維持**——這是原本會壞掉的地方）
- `GOMODCACHE = ~/.local/share/go/pkg/mod`
- `GOCACHE = ~/Library/Caches/go-build`（mac 原生，不動）

實際跑 `go install goimports` / `testscript` → 都落在 `~/.local/bin`，`~/go` 清掉後**不再重生**。

## 計畫外的關鍵發現
驗證時抓到真正的元凶：**mise 會強制 export `GOBIN` 指向自己的版號 toolchain 目錄**（`~/.local/share/mise/installs/go/<ver>/bin`），而且每次 `cd` 都靠 `hook-env` 重新蓋回去——所以光靠 shell 的 `export GOBIN` 會在下一個 prompt 就被打回。更糟的是這代表 `go install` 的 CLI 會在 `go` 升版時整批被清掉。mise 有 `go_set_gopath` / `go_set_goroot` 開關，但**沒有 `go_set_gobin`**。

唯一可靠的解法是在 **mise 自己的 `[env]`** 裡覆寫 `GOBIN`（同一輪 hook-env 套用、優先於 backend 預設）。GOPATH 不用這樣處理，因為 mise 預設 `go_set_gopath=false`，shell 的 export 就穩。

## 改動（8 檔）
| 檔案 | 內容 |
|---|---|
| `dot_config/shell/02_legacy_tools.sh` | `GOPATH → ~/.local/share/go`、`GOBIN → ~/.local/bin`，刪掉失效的 `$GOPATH/bin` PATH 行（非 mise 環境的 fallback）|
| `dot_config/mise/config.toml.tmpl` | **新增 `[env] GOBIN`**（計畫外，元凶修正）|
| `dot_ansible/roles/go_tools/tasks/main.yml` | install task 補 `GOPATH`（避免 build 時重建 `~/go/pkg/mod`）|
| `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh` `cat_go()` | `export GOPATH` 補在 GOBIN 旁 |
| `docs/this_repo/config-conventions.md` + `.zh-TW` | E1 PATH 表：`~/go/bin/` 那列改成 `~/.local/share/go`（GOPATH）|
| `pitfalls/go-install-gobin-resets-to-mise-toolchain-dir.md` + `README.md` | 新增 pitfall（症狀導向，含 mise 無 `go_set_gobin` 這個 gotcha）|

## 驗證
`bash -n` 過、`yq` 解析 YAML 過、`mise doctor` 只有「有新版可更新」這個無關警告、config「No problems found」。
